finding: Exploration-stage company. Seasonal and access delays affected a Kyrgyz drilling programme; no operating mine to assess.
Exploration access and crop-compensation delays affected planned drilling. The downloaded copy is scanned; reviewed a rendered page and readable archived text (printed pp. 10–11).
Feasibility, metallurgy and environmental approvals dominated. No operating-mine production failure was established.
Drilling equipment/ground conditions constrained a Kyrgyz programme. Ayanfuri's acquired historical rehabilitation obligation was recognised.
Exploration-stage priorities included financing, resource confidence and environmental baseline work. Unreliable electricity affected camp food handling.
Development and financing transition: mine approvals and construction financing were priorities. A pending approval is not by itself evidence of a failure.
Edikan construction and Sissingué feasibility/permitting progressed. This year does not establish a repeated mine-closure modelling failure.
Edikan was delivered on time/on budget. Sissingué permitting was temporarily suspended during disputed Ivorian election results, then resumed.
Edikan experienced higher-than-planned unscheduled downtime involving crusher feed, mechanical equipment, water and tailings management; remedial work started.
Crushing-equipment failures and above-budget downtime contributed to production below guidance. Remediation improved crusher availability late in the year.
Processing was interrupted by fire and electricity problems. Lower-grade blending was a deliberate cash-conservation choice; progressive rehabilitation already occurred.
Mandatory grid load shedding prompted standby-generation expansion; full power supply was restored in April. Delayed mining-area access also affected capital work.
Delayed pit approvals/access forced more low-grade stockpile processing and affected output/cost. The company invested in power and plant improvements.
Plant upgrades and relocation were completed; head grade, recovery and production improved. Important evidence of a response, not a persistent identical failure.
Edikan production improved with higher grades/throughput; Sissingué commenced ahead of schedule/on budget. Auditor focus included impairment, revenue and commercial-production timing.
Harder ore reduced Edikan throughput; carbonaceous material affected recovery. Sissingué accelerated waste removal as a precaution after very high rainfall.
A softer/higher-grade Bokitsi blend increased throughput and grade but carbonaceous material reduced recovery. The scanned auditor section's KAM concerned Yaouré development capitalisation.
Recovery improved after Bokitsi depletion, despite lower Edikan output. Closure/rehabilitation provision became a key audit matter, with surveys, rates and mine-plan checks.
Edikan missed output/cost guidance after lower-grade feed, lower throughput and a 19-day preventative shutdown; planning allowance was insufficient. Closure provision remained a KAM.
Edikan output and recovery rebounded and exceeded guidance. Closure provision remained a KAM; the original financial statements were in Australian dollars.

Yaouré mining movements below targets delayed higher-grade ore access. Extreme weather hurt Sissingué's first quarter. Closure provision remained a KAM; reporting switched to USD with restated comparisons.
Yaouré mining performance improved. Nkosuo access/compensation negotiations progressed slower than planned; Sissingué costs exceeded guidance. Closure provision remained a KAM.

Ore-source transitions, lower grades and higher royalties affected production/costs; full-year guidance was achieved. Closure provision remained a KAM. Climate disclosure identified no material current-year weather/supply-chain impact.
